title: Photo-reviewed Bliss Street heritage masses
limitations: Heights, depth of reveals and ornamental dimensions are visual estimates, not architectural surveys.
The full horizontal footprint comes from retained CAD; a single CAD mass may encompass more than one photographed property.
The visible 360 junction splits the historic shop row from the cream tower; unseen tower roof geometry is conservative.
No AI generated facade imagery is used.

buildings.name: Gabled Bliss One and Mini Malik shop row with adjacent cream tower

sourceFacade.baseSource: Facade-local raycast against road/sidewalk mesh; building median only if no ground hit.

review.notes: The low gabled stone shop row is clearly visible across this candidate footprint. Three gable faces span the image, with the left one partly cropped; cars hide the bottom of retail entrances. Full streetward row has two occupied levels; the gabled attic is not counted as another storey.

style.geometryConflict: Observed floors conflict with the retained source height.

observed.roof: Repeated triangular stone gables with small decorative triangular/lobed vents near each peak and very thin roof edge.
observed.upper: Rough pale limestone courses; tall slender rectangular French-door openings with alternating metal grilles and dark open shutters. Long iron balcony runs continuously in front.
observed.ground: Different shop fascias below same historic row: One One Eight, Bliss One and Mini Malik; gray/blue/red storefront bays.
observed.balcony: Shallow slab with thin black vertical railings and visible supporting brackets; no solid balcony parapet.
observed.adjacent: Much taller cream building with orange center strip at right is separate.
observed.bayCountCaveat: Twelve clearly visible narrow upper openings across the row; leftmost edge cropped. Ground shops do not align one-for-one with upper openings.

buildings.dimensionStatus: Photo-estimated heights, openings and ornament; horizontal footprint retained from original CAD roof triangles.
buildings.unobserved: Rear and unphotographed walls are closed plain masonry; room interiors and unseen openings are not reconstructed.

tower.confidence: Approximate six residential levels above retail visible in photo; roof and remaining width run out of frame. Full plan extent comes from retained CAD footprint.

buildings.name: Cream historic house over Dunkin and Le Sam

sourceFacade.baseSource: Facade-local raycast against road/sidewalk mesh; building median only if no ground hit.

review.notes: The cream historic house above Dunkin and Le Sam is clearly visible from roof parapet to retail base. It has two residential floors above ground and distinctive pointed-arch central openings; facade anatomy should preserve these.

style.geometryConflict: Observed floors conflict with the retained source height.

observed.upper: Three central pointed-arch French-door openings per floor with ornate fanlight metalwork; rectangular shuttered windows in outer bays. Black iron balconies join the central triple opening group on each upper floor.
observed.balcony: Shallow concrete slabs on prominent projecting brackets, black thin vertical and ornamental rails; balconies stop before outer shuttered windows.
observed.roof: Flat parapet with thin metal railing and horizontal cornice.
observed.ground: Dunkin left storefront; Le Sam right with yellow-black fascia; three large pointed-arch gray infill panels above right shop.
observed.details: Muted blue-gray louvred shutters opened to each side; wires cross facade.
observed.bayCaveat: Six visual opening groups; three central arches flanked by two rectangular openings at left and one at right.

buildings.name: Bubbles low frontage

sourceFacade.baseSource: Facade-local raycast against road/sidewalk mesh; building median only if no ground hit.

review.notes: The low Bubbles storefront block is visible beside the historic cream corner house. The neighboring green KB Doner sign continues into a separate right-hand frontage; use only the Bubbles extent for this candidate.

style.geometryConflict: Observed floors conflict with the retained source height.

observed.upper: Weathered off-white peeling plaster, rectangular upper openings with tall blue shutters; simple ledge along roof and exposed wiring.
observed.ground: Wide BUBBLES white sign fascia with red stripe, continuous red retractable awning, pale yellow narrow shop supports and glass openings.
observed.occlusion: Van and parked cars obscure lower entrances.
observed.adjacent: Pointed-arch upper windows and green KB Doner fascia are farther right; do not make all Bubbles windows arched.
